summary.title: Talks that changed the way I think about programming
summary.one_liner: A personal list of talks on programming, covering ideas such as simple versus easy, cross-cutting concerns, and questioning software industry assumptions.
takeaways: Simple is not the same as easy; the two should not be confused.
Cross-cutting concerns tend to break encapsulation and tangle object graphs in real programs.
Programming should focus on solving problems rather than on code itself.
Be a critical thinker and check whether adopted practices actually benefit you.
Iterating a 2D array row by row is much faster than column by column.
summary.summary: The post is a personal reading list of talks that shifted the author's views on what good programming is. Each talk is summarized in one line, with no detailed notes, so the list acts as a pointer to the talks themselves. Topics include challenging common claims (software as platform, code over data), the cost of hours spent programming, simplicity versus ease, cross-cutting concerns, memory layout performance, garbage collection and VM tradeoffs, and critiques of the software industry's search for a silver bullet. The page includes an opening quote from Alan Kay about destroying students' beliefs about computing.
